record.paper_title: Open problems, questions and challenges in finite-dimensional integrable systems
record.original_question: Assume that we know explicit formulas for the action variabl es I1,..., In so that we are able to analyse their asymptotic behaviour in a neighb ourhood of a singular fiber. Can we recover the topology of this singularity from the asymptoti c behaviour (or at least to distinguish between different types of singularities)? For example, we know that, in the case of non-degenerate hyperbolic singularities, the singular part Ising is of the form h ln h +.... Is this property characteristic for non-degenerate hyperbolic singularities? The case of one d egree of freedom is understood in [99]. For degenerate singularities, this question becomes, of course, m ore interesting and important. Another interesting problem would be a description of singularities, b oth in local and semi-global setting, which may occur in algebraically integrable systems. There is no commonly accepted definition of algebraic integrability (see discussion on this subject and relevan t definitions in [220]) and the answer may depend on the approach used. In the most natural setting, a lgebraic integrability assumes that the commuting functions F1,..., Fn are polynomials and one can naturally complexify all the related objects (including the phase space, symplectic or Poisson structu re, and time) so that the integrable system under consideration becomes the real part of a certain co mplex integrable system. The crucial additional condition on this complex system is that its general comple x fibers are isomorphic to affine parts of Abelian varieties (see [220]) which imposes rather strong to pological conditions on singularities. For instance, in the case of one degree of freedom, it implies that th e Milnor number of a singular point cannot be greater than 2. In other words, singularities of alg ebraically integrable systems are expected to be very special.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M^{2n}, \omega)$ be a smooth symplectic manifold and let $F = (F_1, \dots, F_n) : M \to \mathbb{R}^n$ be a completely integrable system, i.e., the functions $F_1, \dots, F_n$ are smooth, functionally independent on an open dense set, and pairwise Poisson-commute: $\{F_i, F_j\} = 0$. Near a regular fiber, Arnold–Liouville coordinates yield action variables $I_1(c), \dots, I_n(c)$, where $c = (c_1, \dots, c_n)$ ranges over values of $F$ in a punctured neighbourhood of a critical value corresponding to a singular fiber $F^{-1}(c_0)$.

Assume explicit formulas for the action variables $I_k(c)$ are available, so that their asymptotic expansion as $c \to c_0$ can be analysed. Decompose $I_k$ as $I_k = I_k^{reg} + I_k^{sing}$, where $I_k^{reg}$ is real-analytic at $c_0$ and $I_k^{sing}$ carries the non-smooth part.

(a) Determine to what extent the topology of the singular fiber and of its tubular neighbourhood (the local and semi-local topological type of the singularity, in the sense of the Eliasson–Williamson classification and its degenerate generalizations) is reconstructible from the asymptotic behaviour of $I_k^{sing}(c)$ as $c \to c_0$. In particular, can different topological types of singularities always be distinguished by these asymptotics?

(b) It is known that, for one degree of freedom, a non-degenerate hyperbolic singularity produces a singular part of the form $I^{sing}(h) = h \ln h + \dots$ near the critical value $h = 0$. Prove or disprove: in arbitrary dimension $n$, the appearance of an $h \ln h$-type term in $I_k^{sing}$ is a characteristic property of non-degenerate hyperbolic singularities (and singularities containing a hyperbolic block).

(c) Investigate the analogous question for degenerate singularities: classify the possible asymptotic forms of action variables near degenerate singular fibers and relate them to the topology of the singularity.

(d) Describe which local and semi-local singularities can occur in algebraically integrable systems, in the following sense: $F_1, \dots, F_n$ are polynomials on $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$, the system admits a complexification to a complex integrable system whose generic complex fibers are isomorphic to affine parts of abelian varieties. (For one degree of freedom this restricts the Milnor number of a singular point to be at most $2$.) Provide a classification of admissible singularity types in this algebraic setting.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is listed as an open problem in a 2018 survey on finite-dimensional integrable systems by Bolsinov, Izosimov, and Tsonev (zbMath 7030249). I found no subsequent work resolving the higher-dimensional characterization of non-degenerate hyperbolic singularities via action-variable asymptotics, nor a complete classification of singularities in algebraically integrable systems. The one-degree-of-freedom case is treated in earlier literature, but the multidimensional and degenerate cases appear to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Open problems, questions and challenges in finite-dimensional integrable systems
status_evidence.snippet: Section 2 collects open questions on action variables and singular fibers of integrable systems, including the asymptotic characterization of hyperbolic singularities.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is posed as an open question in the survey.
